subject: Customer request: Clarify data use boundaries, no-training commitment, and evidence
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@healthsolutions.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@healthsolutions.com, Maya Singh <maya.singh@healthsolutions.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify data use boundaries and no-training terms

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the call yesterday. As we move this toward procurement, Legal and Security asked us to get explicit answers on three items before we can sign: 

1) A clear no-training / no-model-improvement commitment for data sent via API (including examples of what counts as "use for model improvement").
2) A copy of the current subprocessors list and whether any of them perform model training or aggregated analytics that could be considered model improvement.
3) Evidence that customer prompt/response data can be exported and deleted on demand, and whether any backups or analytics stores contain retained copies.

Can you confirm you can provide a DPA addendum with the no-training clause and the attachments above? Also please include a single-point summary (one page) our security team can consume quickly.

We need this by EOD Thursday to keep the timeline.

Thanks,
Tom Rivera
Head of IT Risk, HealthSolutions

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@healthsolutions.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify data use boundaries and no-training terms

Tom — thank you and great to meet yesterday. We can absolutely provide the artifacts you requested. Quick plan: 

- I will attach a draft DPA addendum with a narrow no-training commitment and a companion one-page evidence summary.
- Dev, can you attach the current subprocessor inventory and confirm whether any subprocessors perform model training or hold persistent copies of prompt/response data?
- Priyom, can you prepare a brief description of our export/delete flows (SFTP, API export, retention windows) plus the backup snapshot policy.

Tom — our standard hosted offering commits to not use customer-provided data for model improvement unless explicitly opted in (we are happy to add clarified language into the DPA addendum). We do rely on a small set of third-party metrics providers (for telemetry) but we will confirm they do not do training or retain PII in a form used for model training.

Can we do a short 30-minute call tomorrow 09:00 PT to review the addendum and the evidence pack? If that works I will send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@healthsolutions.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify data use boundaries and no-training terms

Tom / Ava — attaching three items (see stub attachments): 

- subprocessors_2027-05-18.xlsx (stub): current vendor inventory with roles and data access scope. Columns: vendor, role, access_type, holds_persistent_prompt_data, performs_model_training.
- no-train-evidence-summary.txt (stub): brief notes on technical controls — request routing that strips opt-out signals, KV cache TTLs, model improvement pipeline exclusion, and telemetry aggregation.
- DPA_HealthSolutions_v2.pdf (stub): DPA with addendum language [Section 7.3].

Summary answers inline: 
- No listed subprocessor performs model training on customer prompt/response data. The model training work is performed only on internal training corpora and explicitly segregated datasets. 
- Hosted backups: we retain short-term snapshots for disaster recovery (encrypted at rest); we will include an export that removes customer records on deletion requests and rotate keys per policy. Backups older than 90 days are rotated and purged per our retention policy, and we can provide attestation. 
- Export options: API export (bulk), SFTP push to HealthSolutions-owned bucket, and an ad-hoc export packaged for legal review.

I can join the call tomorrow and walk through the subprocessor sheet and technical notes.

--
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@healthsolutions.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@healthsolutions.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify data use boundaries and no-training terms

Thanks — quick confirmation from our side after scanning the attachments: 

- The DPA addendum language looks acceptable in principle but Legal needs a single tracked-change version that explicitly states: "Customer data, including prompts and generated responses, will not be used to improve models nor used as training data unless Customer provides documented opt-in." Please include that exact phrasing in the next draft.
- Can you produce the attestation for backups and key rotation (signed) and confirm whether any telemetry aggregates are ever stored outside our region?
- Finally, can you put the subprocessor sheet under a brief NDA (we prefer redacted public-facing list + full sheet under NDA).

If you can get the tracked-change DPA and the signed backup attestation by EOD Thursday we'll route to procurement. Call invite for 9:00 PT tomorrow is on my calendar.

Best,
Maya Singh
Sr. Counsel, HealthSolutions
